_comment: MEH-1800 — the registry of search-input placeholder strings that must stay
answerable by the live search. ONE list, read by BOTH halves of the guard:
· frontend/__tests__/SearchPlaceholderContract.test.js (structural, blocking)
· scripts/check_placeholder_search.py                  (live data, periodic)
Two copies of this list would drift, and a key silently dropped from one of
them is exactly the silent-coverage-gap class .claude/rules/testing.md warns
about under 'Guarded registries'.
Add a key here when you add a placeholder that teaches the user what the
search field accepts. Do NOT add placeholders for fields that are not the
site search (admin filters, form inputs) — they are not search queries and
the live half would fail them for the wrong reason.
KNOWN GAP, stated so it is not mistaken for coverage: this registry lists
he.json ONLY. Every en.json counterpart returns 0 on staging — including
the four MEH-1690 shipped ('Sourdough bread', 'Breads and baking',
'Zichron Yaakov', "Ma'afiyat HaMachmetzet") — because producer, product,
city and category names are all Hebrew, so NO English string returns a
result for ANY scope. That is a whole-locale gap, not a bad string: it
cannot be fixed by picking better English copy, and adding these keys here
would red the guard permanently with no fix available. Reported under
MEH-1800; the decision (transliterate names? search Hebrew from /en?) is
product's, not this guard's.
